newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates steady in routine end-year trade.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates steady in routine end-year trade.

text.p: Dutch money market rates held steady in routine end-of-year trade on Monday, with most activity concentrated in overnight guilders, dealers said.

"There have been a lot of deals in call money, which is customary for this time of year," one dealer said, adding that the majority of business was being done at around 2.88 percent, more or less unchanged from Friday.
Trade in longer-dated deposits was minimal, although some deals had been done in one-month money, dealers said. One-month deposits were quoted at an unchanged 2.98 percent bid.
Others said the finance ministry's agent had placed more Dutch Treasury Certificates (DTCs) under its February programme.
"We did some deals at 3.0 percent in February DTCs, for payment on January 10," one dealer said.
The finance ministry had 4.46 billion guilders outstanding under its February programme on December 9.

Asked to comment on speculation the German Bundesbank could be looking to trim its repo rate at its pre-Christmas meeting after the recent drop in retail sales volumes and limited inflation, most dealers said they regarded a move as unlikely.
"Of course one cannot rule it out, but I've heard nothing to that effect," one dealer said.
The Bundesbank is due to meet this Thursday.
The guilder held steady against the mark, quoting at 112.195 per 100 marks from Friday's fixing of 112.190.
